run.question: Use the custom-crd runbook and check why custom CRD whale-watcher resources are not being reconciled by the operator in namespace app-96

report.summary: The requested runbook 'custom-crd' was not available to this target (fetch_skill returned KNOWLEDGE_NOT_FOUND and named only 'service-troubleshooting' as available), so its steps could not be followed. The custom CRD itself is registered and healthy-looking: whalewatchers.ocean.io (group ocean.io, kind WhaleWatcher, Namespaced, single version v1 served=true/storage=true, conversion None, Established=True, NamesAccepted=True/NoConflicts) was created 2026-11-21T07:32:31Z and declares no status subresource. The operator workload app-96/whale-operator is a Deployment (generation 1, revision 1, created 2026-11-21T07:32:31Z, 1 of 1 ready) whose pod whale-operator-5f695b7c66-kd5lj is Running and Ready, restartCount 0, running 'python /app/operator.py' with code from a Secret volume under ServiceAccount whale-operator. The only RBAC path for that ServiceAccount is ClusterRole/ClusterRoleBinding 'whale-operator', which grants only get, list and watch on ocean.io/whalewatchers — no update, patch or create verb and no whalewatchers/status rule; because the CRD has no status subresource, recording status.phase/lastSeen/observationCount requires update on the whalewatchers resource. That read-only permission is the leading hypothesis for CRs never showing a reconciled status, but it is unconfirmed: the operator's stdout/stderr returned no lines, the operator code Secret is unreadable, the WhaleWatcher objects cannot be listed with the available tooling, and Prometheus and Jaeger were both SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no metric or trace evidence exists. A second open candidate is timing: the namespace, CRD, ServiceAccount, ClusterRole, binding and Deployment were all created at 2026-11-21T07:32:31Z, roughly 38 seconds before the sampled window end, with the operator process starting 07:32:32Z, so the window holds no earlier state to date the non-reconciliation. Only six events exist in the window, all Normal startup events; none names a WhaleWatcher. No impact on any other workload was observed, and none is claimed.

claims.text: CustomResourceDefinition whalewatchers.ocean.io exists with group ocean.io, kind WhaleWatcher, plural whalewatchers, scope Namespaced, single version v1 (served=true, storage=true), conversion strategy None, and conditions Established=True (reason InitialNamesAccepted) and NamesAccepted=True (reason NoConflicts); the version declares spec and status schemas but no subresources block, i.e. no status subresource.
The CRD whalewatchers.ocean.io carries creationTimestamp 2026-11-21T07:32:31Z, about 38 seconds before the sampled window end of 2026-11-21T07:33:09Z.

Deployment app-96/whale-operator has spec.replicas 1 with status 1 ready and 1 available, generation 1, deployment revision 1, created 2026-11-21T07:32:31Z; its container 'operator' runs command ['python','/app/operator.py'] on image python:3.9-slim, mounts volume 'operator-code' from a Secret at /app, has resources limits cpu 100m / memory 128Mi and requests cpu 50m / memory 64Mi, and runs under serviceAccountName whale-operator with OPERATOR_NAMESPACE taken from the pod's metadata.namespace.

In namespace app-96 the only pod is whale-operator-5f695b7c66-kd5lj: phase Running, all conditions True (PodReadyToStartContainers, Initialized, Ready, ContainersReady, PodScheduled), startTime 2026-11-21T07:32:31Z, container 'operator' ready=true, restartCount=0, state running since 2026-11-21T07:32:32Z, imageID docker.io/library/import-2026-11-20@sha256:e46cb38190671c6c91fff131411c5a6ae3dbbcde1653579afe6fe22d119530b9, lastState empty.

Ownership chain for the operator pod is Pod whale-operator-5f695b7c66-kd5lj -> ReplicaSet whale-operator-5f695b7c66 (replicas 1, ready 1, created 2026-11-21T07:32:31Z, pod-template-hash 5f695b7c66, owner Deployment whale-operator); it is the only ReplicaSet in app-96, so no earlier ReplicaSet of this Deployment is visible.

ClusterRole whale-operator (created 2026-11-21T07:32:31Z) contains exactly one rule: apiGroups ['ocean.io'], resources ['whalewatchers'], verbs ['get','list','watch'] — it grants no update, patch, create or delete verb and no rule for the whalewatchers/status subresource.

ClusterRoleBinding whale-operator binds ClusterRole whale-operator to ServiceAccount whale-operator in namespace app-96, and it is the only ClusterRoleBinding in the cluster whose subjects reference namespace app-96.
ServiceAccount whale-operator exists in app-96 (created 2026-11-21T07:32:31Z), so the operator pod's serviceAccountName resolves; the only other ServiceAccount in the namespace is 'default'.

All six events whose timestamps fall inside the authorized window, across all namespaces, are Normal events in app-96 for operator startup: Deployment whale-operator ScalingReplicaSet ('Scaled up replica set whale-operator-5f695b7c66 from 0 to 1', 07:32:31Z), ReplicaSet whale-operator-5f695b7c66 SuccessfulCreate, and Pod whale-operator-5f695b7c66-kd5lj Scheduled (07:32:31Z) / Pulled / Created / Started (07:32:32Z); none involves a WhaleWatcher object and none is a Warning, FailedScheduling or Unhealthy event.
Namespace app-96 itself was created 2026-11-21T07:32:31Z and its phase is Active, and Deployment whale-operator is the only Deployment cluster-wide whose name contains 'whale'.

The operator container is not crash-looping: restartCount is 0, lastState is empty, and the container has been running continuously since 2026-11-21T07:32:32Z, so a container-level crash loop or OOMKill is not what is keeping CRs from being reconciled (no Evicted, OOMKilled or BackOff evidence exists for this pod).

CRD registration is not the failure point: whalewatchers.ocean.io reports Established=True and NamesAccepted=True with reason NoConflicts, and its v1 version is served and is the storage version, so the API server is serving the WhaleWatcher type.

Leading hypothesis: whale-operator cannot write reconciliation results because its authorization is read-only. ClusterRole whale-operator grants only get/list/watch on ocean.io/whalewatchers with no update or patch verb and no whalewatchers/status rule, while the CRD declares no status subresource, so writing status.phase, status.lastSeen or status.observationCount requires update on the whalewatchers resource itself; such writes would be rejected as Forbidden (403) and the WhaleWatcher objects would never show a reconciled status. This could not be confirmed from operator error output in this Run.

Alternative candidate still open: the reported non-reconciliation may be a timing artefact of a brand-new install. Namespace app-96, the whalewatchers.ocean.io CRD, ServiceAccount whale-operator, ClusterRole and ClusterRoleBinding whale-operator, and Deployment whale-operator were all created at 2026-11-21T07:32:31Z, and the operator process started only at 07:32:32Z, so any CR created before that had no running controller and the sampled window contains no earlier state to compare against; this does not by itself explain continued non-reconciliation after startup.

Alternative candidate still open: the operator application logic itself (loaded from the Secret volume 'operator-code' mounted at /app, whose Secret name is redacted in the Deployment spec) may not reconcile correctly — it could be blocked, swallowing errors, or watching a different scope; the code could not be read, so this cannot be confirmed or excluded.

Grant the write verbs a controller needs: extend ClusterRole whale-operator with update and patch on ocean.io/whalewatchers (and add a whalewatchers/status rule), then verify with 'kubectl auth can-i patch whalewatchers.ocean.io --as=system:serviceaccount:app-96:whale-operator -n app-96'; alternatively enable the CRD's status subresource so status writes use whalewatchers/status.

Make the operator's diagnostics readable before concluding: run the container with PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 (or 'python -u') so its stdout/stderr reach the log stream, and have a human with Secret read access confirm that the 'operator-code' Secret contains an operator.py that watches WhaleWatchers in app-96 and performs the expected status write.

Confirm the failure directly with read access to the custom resource: list the WhaleWatcher objects in app-96 and check whether status.phase, status.lastSeen and status.observationCount are populated and whether resourceVersion changes over time, and correlate with an apiserver audit entry showing a 403 for system:serviceaccount:app-96:whale-operator.

gaps: The 'custom-crd' runbook does not exist for this target: fetch_skill returned KNOWLEDGE_NOT_FOUND (status error, not citable) and listed only 'service-troubleshooting' as available, so no custom-crd runbook step could be attempted and no step can be reported as blocked by a missing tool.

Prometheus was unavailable for this Run: metrics_range_query of kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{namespace="app-96"}, kube_pod_container_info{namespace="app-96"} and kube_replicaset_owner{namespace="app-96"}, and execute_prometheus_instant_query of 'up', each returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (status error). No metric series exists as evidence, including kube-state-metrics deployment and restart history and any error-rate or ERROR series; object history before the sampled instant 2026-11-21T07:33:09Z is unknown, not zero.
Jaeger was unavailable: traces_list_services returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (status error), so no trace evidence exists for this Run and nothing can be said about trace spans or callers of the operator.

The WhaleWatcher custom resources themselves could not be read: kubernetes_tabular_query with kind=whalewatchers was refused with INVALID_PARAMS (status error), so whether any WhaleWatcher objects exist in app-96, their spec and status, and whether they are actually unreconciled remain unverified; the question's premise could not be checked directly.

The operator's stdout/stderr are empty: fetch_pod_logs for whale-operator-5f695b7c66-kd5lj returned 0 lines (status no_data) for both the default one-hour read and the explicit 2026-11-21T07:32:00Z-07:33:09Z window, with 'no previous instance' for the container. An empty read is not proof that nothing was logged (Python buffers stdout when not attached to a tty), so no 403/Forbidden or other runtime error line could be observed, and the previous container's logs do not exist.

The operator code cannot be inspected: it is mounted from the Secret volume 'operator-code' whose Secret name is redacted in the Deployment spec, and Secrets are not readable with these tools, so the reconciliation logic, watch scope, namespace selection and error handling are unverified.

Queries for roles and rolebindings in app-96 returned no items (views status no_data, not citable), so the absence of additional namespaced RBAC bindings in app-96 is unchecked rather than established.

Queries for validatingwebhookconfigurations and mutatingwebhookconfigurations returned no items (views status no_data, not citable), so whether an admission webhook could be rejecting WhaleWatcher writes is unchecked.

Queries for services and resourcequotas in app-96 returned no items (views status no_data, not citable), so their absence is not established and quota or service configuration cannot be ruled in or out.

No history exists before 2026-11-21T07:32:31Z for this stack: the namespace, CRD, ServiceAccount, RBAC objects and Deployment were all created at that instant and the operator process started 07:32:32Z, so there is no baseline showing when reconciliation stopped or that it ever worked.

Only six events are retained in the authorized window (07:32:31Z-07:32:32Z), all Normal startup events; events that expired or have null timestamps are unknown, and no retained event names a WhaleWatcher object.
The change_history integration is not available to this Run, so no deployment or configuration change record exists to date any rollout or RBAC edit.
next_steps: Have a human with Secret and custom-resource read access inspect the 'operator-code' Secret and list WhaleWatcher objects (spec and status) in app-96 to confirm the non-reconciliation and capture the operator's error output.

Re-check Prometheus once reachable: kube_deployment_status_replicas_available, kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total and kube_pod_container_info for namespace app-96, to date any restart or rollout relative to the alert.

Run the operator with unbuffered stdout/stderr (or a log-file sidecar) so the next occurrence leaves diagnostic evidence, and inspect apiserver audit records for 403 responses for system:serviceaccount:app-96:whale-operator on ocean.io/whalewatchers.

If write permission is the cause, apply the ClusterRole change and confirm with 'kubectl auth can-i update whalewatchers.ocean.io --as=system:serviceaccount:app-96:whale-operator -n app-96' before re-testing reconciliation.
